card.title: 12th UŁAN
card.flavorText: The 12th Podolian Uhlan Regiment was one of Poland’s most storied cavalry units, tracing its traditions back to Napoleonic times and fighting continuously for Polish independence and survival across generations. Officially re-formed in 1919, the regiment distinguished itself in the Polish–Soviet War, taking part in major cavalry actions such as the Battle of Komarów, one of the largest cavalry engagements of the 20th century. During the interwar years, the 12th Uhlans were stationed in Volhynia and became part of Poland’s mobile cavalry forces, combining traditional horsemanship with modern tactics. In September 1939, the regiment was mobilized as part of the Wołyń Cavalry Brigade and fought fiercely against German armored units during the opening battles of the invasion of Poland, including actions around Mokra. Though forced to destroy their regimental flag to prevent its capture after the Soviet invasion, the legacy of the 12th Uhlans endured. It was reformed later within the Polish forces fighting alongside the Allies, but by then the unit had been transformed into infantry. The regiment went on to fight in Italy, earning lasting renown at Monte Cassino in 1944. In October 1946, it embarked from Naples and was transported to Great Britain, where it was officially disbanded on May 6, 1947.
